title: Asset and Drop
premise: Lena Quintana, a former forensic auditor turned whistle-blower, has spent three years buried under four identities after testifying against the Halcyon Group, a logistics conglomerate that launders money for arms dealers. When a burner phone arrives containing recordings of her own erased memories—and a voice she recognizes as her dead brother Marco—the calls reveal that Halcyon plans to destroy a ferry carrying evidence of their crimes, staging it as an accident on the anniversary of the incident that killed Marco. As Lena races to decode the phone's origin, she discovers Marco may have faked his death to build the case she was too broken to finish, and that her handler in witness protection has been feeding Halcyon her location all along. In the end, Lena chooses truth over safety: she boards the ferry, broadcasts the evidence live, saves the passengers but loses Marco for real this time, and walks out of witness protection into a public reckoning—finally able to sleep.
about_author: Theo Fairweather is a former maritime insurance investigator who spent a decade reconstructing accidents nobody wanted called crimes. He writes thrillers about people whose careful lives are dismantled by one impossible phone call.

chapters.title: Four Names
chapters.summary: POV: Lena. In her fourth identity as 'Karen Voss,' a night-shift bookkeeper in Duluth, Lena catalogs her insomnia rituals and the rules that keep her invisible. A small slip—a coworker calling her by a name from her second life—rattles her. Emotional beat: the exhausting vigilance of a woman who has forgotten what unguarded feels like.

chapters.title: The Package That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: POV: Lena. A padded envelope with no return address appears inside her locked mailbox: a burner phone, charged, with one contact saved as M. She almost destroys it, then hears the voice on the voicemail preview—Marco's, unmistakable, saying a phrase only he used. Emotional beat: grief cracked open by impossibility.

chapters.title: Dead Men Don't Dial
chapters.summary: POV: Lena. Lena verifies Marco's death certificate through a records contact, confirming he died in the Halcyon warehouse fire three years ago—the same fire she survived and testified about. The phone rings. She answers. Marco says: 'You have eleven days.' Emotional beat: terror braided with desperate hope.

chapters.title: Handler
chapters.summary: POV: Lena. Her US Marshal handler, Dale Pruitt, checks in for his monthly review and notices her agitation. Lena conceals the phone but realizes Pruitt knows details of her apartment layout he shouldn't. Emotional beat: the slow horror of suspecting your protector.

chapters.title: Eleven Days
chapters.summary: POV: Lena. Marco explains in fragments: an attack scheduled for the tenth anniversary of the warehouse fire, staged as an accident aboard the Lake Superior ferry Aurora Star, which will carry a retired Halcyon accountant holding a ledger copy. He can't say where he is. Emotional beat: mission focus as anesthesia for grief.

chapters.title: The Ledger Keeper
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Lena / the accountant, Ruth Ibarra. Ruth, packing for a cruise she believes is a reward, finds a note slipped into her luggage warning her not to board. Ruth's chapters give the target a face. Emotional beat: two women unknowingly converging on the same water.

chapters.title: What the Fire Took
chapters.summary: POV: Lena, in flashback-heavy reflection triggered by the phone's first recording: audio of the warehouse fire night that includes sounds Lena's traumatized memory deleted—including Marco alive after the explosion. Emotional beat: memory as unreliable architecture; the past rearranging itself.

chapters.title: Tail Lights on Superior Street
chapters.summary: POV: Lena. Someone follows her home from work. She runs counter-surveillance drills Marco taught her and identifies a gray sedan with government plates. She photographs it; the plate belongs to a vehicle reported destroyed. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into method.

chapters.title: Pruitt's Second Phone
chapters.summary: POV: Lena. Using a library computer, Lena traces a duplicate burner number that has pinged near her apartment for months—it matches a number in old case files belonging to Pruitt. Her handler is selling her coordinates. Emotional beat: betrayal confirmed; the safe house concept dies.

chapters.title: Run Quiet
chapters.summary: POV: Lena. Lena abandons identity four mid-shift, executing a pre-planned extraction route she built years ago and never hoped to use. She burns 'Karen Voss' in a dumpster fire and drives north through sleet toward Duluth's harbor. Emotional beat: grim liberation—running toward something at last.

chapters.title: Ruth Boards Anyway
chapters.summary: POV: Ruth Ibarra. Ruth dismisses the warning note as a prank, but pockets the ledger out of stubbornness—her late husband's pension depends on Halcyon honoring its settlements. She boards the Aurora Star. Emotional beat: ordinary courage in a woman who doesn't know she's bait.

chapters.title: The Voice on the Water
chapters.summary: POV: Lena. From a motel above the harbor, Marco guides her to a maintenance locker key taped under a pier bench: inside, a radio, schematics of the ferry, and a photo of the saboteur—a Halcyon fixer named Corliss whom Lena once saw at the courthouse. Emotional beat: trust rekindled, tested by distance.

chapters.title: Corliss
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Lena / Corliss. Corliss preps the sabotage—fuel-line tampering disguised as corrosion—while musing that accidents are kinder than murders. His professionalism chills; his contempt for 'assets' like Lena clarifies the stakes. Emotional beat: meeting the antagonist's calm and hating how reasonable it sounds.

chapters.title: Nine Hours
chapters.summary: POV: Lena. The ferry departs at dawn with 212 aboard. Marco's line goes silent except for a countdown he refuses to explain. Lena realizes the attack isn't just destruction—it's timed to a live Halcyon board call, an alibi broadcast. Emotional beat: the clock becoming a character.

chapters.title: Ticket for One
chapters.summary: POV: Lena. Lena buys a same-day ticket using her real name for the first time in three years—a deliberate signal to whoever is watching. She boards the Aurora Star carrying the ledger photos Marco transmitted and a plan with more holes than hull. Emotional beat: choosing exposure over safety, finally.

chapters.title: Below Decks
chapters.summary: POV: Lena. In the engine room, Lena finds Corliss's tampering half-complete and must choose: disable the bomb and lose the proof of intent, or document everything first. She does both, badly, and trips a pressure sensor. Emotional beat: competence fraying under real stakes.

chapters.title: Anniversary
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Lena / Ruth. The ship shudders; alarms. Ruth, recognizing Lena from a decade-old deposition photo, presses the physical ledger into her hands—'I carried it this far.' Passengers stampede toward decks. Emotional beat: strangers entrusting each other with the truth.

chapters.title: Corliss at the Rail
chapters.summary: POV: Lena. Corliss corners Lena on the aft deck; the fight is short, ugly, and ends when Ruth strikes him with a lifeboat oar and he goes over the rail into black water. Marco's voice returns on the burner: 'Engine room. Now. It wasn't me who set the timer.' Emotional beat: victory curdling into new dread.

chapters.title: The Second Timer
chapters.summary: POV: Lena. In the flooding engine room, Lena finds a second device on an independent trigger—Pruitt's insurance policy, meant to sink the evidence along with the ship regardless of Corliss's success. Marco talks her through defusal while admitting he's been on the ferry since Duluth. Emotional beat: revelation and countdown fused.

chapters.title: Marco
chapters.summary: POV: Lena. She finds him in the cargo hold, burned and dying—he never fully escaped the fire three years ago; he's been building the case from hiding ever since, and the phone was his way of finishing it through her. With the timer dead and the ferry limping to shore, he makes her promise to testify again. Emotional beat: the reunion that is also a farewell.

chapters.title: Everything Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV: Lena. Docked under emergency lights, Lena streams the ledger, the schematics, and her own testimony to every feed she can find before Halcyon's lawyers can move. Federal agents arrest Pruitt on the pier. Ruth stands beside her as witness. Emotional beat: truth as a flare fired into open sky.

chapters.title: One Name, Hers
chapters.summary: POV: Lena. Weeks later, at Marco's funeral held under his real name, Lena declines new identities and signs her lease with her own signature. That night she sleeps eight hours and wakes without checking the locks. Emotional beat: inheritance claimed—not of fear, but of the fight he left her.
